questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.learningObjective: Explain the difference between peak and peak-to-peak
questions.stem: While fixing a common mistake, explain the difference between peak and peak-to-peak voltage.

answer.exemplar: Peak voltage is the maximum displacement from zero, while peak-to-peak is the total span from the negative peak to the positive peak, equal to twice the peak for a symmetric sinusoid.

questions.explanation: Peak-to-peak spans both extremes, so it is twice the peak for a symmetric wave. A tempting mistake is to read peak-to-peak as the peak value.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.topic: Why the root-mean-square value is quoted
questions.learningObjective: Explain why rms is used for power calculations
questions.stem: While fixing a common mistake, why is the rms value of an AC voltage quoted for heating effect?

answer.exemplar: The rms value delivers the same average power to a resistor as a DC voltage of that value, because power depends on V squared averaged over time.

questions.explanation: Average power is proportional to mean V^2, whose square root is the rms value. Quoting peak would overstate the heating effect.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.learningObjective: Explain why resistor voltage and current are in phase

answer.exemplar: Ohm's law V = IR holds instantaneously for a resistor, so when current is maximum voltage is maximum; no energy storage means no phase shift.

questions.explanation: A resistor stores no energy, so V and I peak together. Capacitors and inductors store energy and create phase shifts.

questions.learningObjective: Explain the frequency dependence of capacitive reactance
questions.stem: While fixing a common mistake, explain why capacitive reactance decreases as frequency increases.

answer.exemplar: X_C = 1/(2 pi f C), so as f rises the denominator grows and X_C falls; a capacitor passes high frequencies more easily because it has less time to charge.

answer.exemplar: X_L = 2 pi f L, so as f rises X_L rises; an inductor opposes faster current changes more strongly.

questions.explanation: R and X are perpendicular legs; |Z| is the hypotenuse. A tempting mistake is to add R and X arithmetically.

questions.learningObjective: Compute phase angle for a capacitive load
questions.stem: While fixing a common mistake, R = 40 ohms, X_L = 0, X_C = 30 ohms. Find the phase angle in degrees.
